item.description:
Cartea, A., Chang, P., Garcia Arenas, G.
We propose a dynamic model of the limit order book to derive conditions to test whether it is optimal to manipulate the order book. Our results show that as a market maker becomes more tolerant to bearing inventory risk, optimal strategies that manipulate the book occur more frequently. Manipulation helps to revert inventory to an optimal level and to execute round-trip trades with limit orders at a higher probability than was otherwise likely to occur. item.description:
Schneeberger, A., Krupka, E.
What determines whether someone complies with a social norm? The social identity approach offers a mechanism for norm compliance: A person who feels similar to a group identifies more with that group and, in turn, complies with the group’s norms. Using an experiment, we test whether similarity in values increases identification and adherence to a group rule. item.title: Screening, Investment Incentives, and the Welfare Trade-Offs of Privacy
item.description:
Dosis, A., Rothschild, C.
This paper studies how information disclosure affects investment incentives and contracting efficiency. We analyze a class of principal-agent models in which information helps the principal screen the agent but also facilitates surplus appropriation, thereby weakening the agent’s incentive to invest before contracting. item.description:
Gurun, U., Liu, Z., Xiao, S.
The rising dominance of superplatforms raises concerns about conflicts of interest and externalities on innovation, because they act as both marketplace gatekeepers and strategic investors. Studying Google’s dual role via Google Ventures (GV) and the Android marketplace, we find Google-backed startups receive 115% more reviews, 12% higher ratings, and 77% fewer bug complaints than their iOS counterparts—despite no major app updates. item.description:

Measures of overconfidence are used both to assess biases in people’s beliefs regarding their own abilities and to identify correlates of those biases. Proposed correlates of overconfidence include narcissism, social status, (low) task anxiety, savings, planning, and many more. item.title: Stockouts and the Success of New Products
item.description:
Aparicio, D., Simester, D.
We investigate how stockouts of existing products influence the success of new product introductions. Our findings reveal that stockouts on incumbent items at the time a new product is launched are associated with higher sales of the new product for at least six months. item.description:
Chen, C., Qian, P., Zhang, J.
In decentralized dynamic matching markets, agents can benefit from sharing resources, but they will collaborate only if properly incentivized. Motivated by applications such as multihospital kidney exchanges and job-hunting markets, this paper proposes novel monetary and nonmonetary mechanisms to incentivize collaboration in such decentralized dynamic markets. item.title: Proximity-Based Delivery Policies: Efficiency, Coverage, and Fairness
item.description:
Wang, Z., Cui, S., Li, Y., Zhang, Q.
The growing demand for rapid food and grocery delivery has prompted many restaurants and retailers to develop their own on-demand delivery services. Although hiring additional couriers can expand delivery capacity, it is often prohibitively costly. As a cost-effective alternative, we propose a proximity-based delivery (PBD) policy that prioritizes the delivery of orders from customers located closer to the vendor, in contrast to the traditional first-come-first-served (FCFS) approach. We develop a deep learning framework to directly estimate tangency portfolio weights by augmenting benchmark factors with a long-short deep factor derived from high-dimensional characteristics. Guided by a Sharpe ratio maximization objective, the deep factor plays two key roles: (i) providing a natural hedge against benchmark risks and (ii) capturing multimarket signals to enhance the performance of the benchmark. item.description:
Ding, H., Wu, M., Yin, Y., Yang, H.
This study investigates periodic travel behavior in a bimodal system under a credit charge-cum-reward scheme, a periodic mobility management system. Our model integrates routine daily commuting with uncertain stop-making activities, which introduce day-level uncertainty. This paper proposes two categories of fixed- and finite-time update rules to enhance the convergence of distributed optimal power flow (OPF) solved using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). item.description:

As live-stream e-commerce rapidly expands and gains popularity among consumers, many brand owners have supplemented their self-owned direct-selling channels with live-stream selling channels to utilize social network effects of key opinion leaders (KOLs). item.description:
Bhardwaj, A., Akkermans, H., Van Wassenhove, L.
Man-made disasters are always shocking, especially when they involve loss of life. The shock is even greater when such disasters are attributed to failures in highly regulated organizations like Boeing, long known for engineering excellence and safety. item.description:
Tomas Ortega, Hamid Jafarkhani
We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. item.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Soft-Constrained AC-OPF in Multiphase Distribution Systems
item.description:
Hoang T. Nguyen, Deepjyoti Deka, Priya L. Donti, Varsha Pendyala, Nurali Virani et al.
This paper presents a self-supervised learning framework for fast, soft-constrained AC optimal power flow (OPF) in unbalanced multiphase distribution systems. The soft AC-OPF objective balances operating cost, renewable energy curtailment, and penalties for violating operating limits. item.title: Congestion-Aware Adaptive Routing for LLM Classification
item.description:
Yuan Guo, Stefanus Jasin, Chen-An Lin
Organizations use large language models (LLMs) to classify jobs that differ in uncertainty and the cost of errors. Querying additional models may improve accuracy, but it also incurs fees and increases congestion at shared servers. We study congestion-aware adaptive routing (CAAR) policies that adapt model selection and stopping decisions to observed outputs while accounting for the steady-state congestion they generate. item.description:
Ramazan G. Beden
In this paper, we investigate left-invariant intrinsic chronometers (time functions) on connected finite-dimensional Lie groups. We formulate and prove sub-Lorentzian analogs of V.\,N.\,Berestovskii's classical direct and inverse theorems. item.description:
Dawid Lipinski, Maciej Buze
The annealed Sinkhorn algorithm is an iterative method for approximating solutions of optimal transport problems, in which the entropic regularisation parameter is progressively decreased. As this parameter decreases, one may preserve either the multiplicative scaling factors or the corresponding dual potentials. Balázs Gerencsér, Miklós Kornyik
In this work we establish an upper bound on the almost sure convergence rate of a broad class of push-sum algorithms, more precisely for those where message passing events follow a Markovian dynamics, or a Hidden Markov Model. item.description:
Jelena Diakonikolas, Guy Kornowski
We settle the deterministic oracle complexity of packing and covering linear programs, as measured by the number of oracle queries to the constraint matrix modeled by left and right matrix-vector products, up to a logarithmic factor. We do so by providing nearly-matching upper and lower bounds. item.description:
Guangyi He, Damir Filipovic, Lukas Gonon
Random feature neural networks (RFNNs) sample their hidden parameters once and train only the output layer. We analyze RFNNs as feedback policies for finite-horizon stochastic control with trajectory-dependent objectives. A policy change alters later states, so the error that matters is the objective error of the induced trajectory rather than a pointwise regression error. item.description:
Francisco Moreno-Mora, Stefan Streif
Value iteration is an important tool for approximating solutions of infinite-horizon optimal control problems, but in practice it is never carried out exactly: value functions are represented by finite-dimensional approximators, and the iteration is stopped after finitely many steps. item.description:
Zhao Song, Ruizhe Zhang
We construct a matrix analog of the Lee-Sidford barrier for semidefinite programming (SDP) with $m$ equality constraints and $n$-by-$n$ matrices. item.description:
Maximilian von Aspern, Andreas S. Schulz, Eugenio Vairo
We present a new linear programming relaxation for minimizing the total weighted completion time on identical parallel machines. Its right-hand side is supermodular, so the relaxation can be solved by a greedy algorithm. We show that the WSPT rule is within a factor $\frac{1}{2}(1 + \sqrt{2})$ of the optimal LP value. item.title: Learning and Dynamic Route Recommendation Under Unknown Traveler Compliance and Road Conditions
item.description:
Yanru Guo, Siqian Shen, Ruiwei Jiang, Xi Jessie Yang
Route planning during evacuations and other large-scale egress operations is inherently dynamic: the planner's recommendations affect future congestion on the roads, influence whether travelers accept their guidance, and determine what the planner can learn from the travelers' actual route choices. item.description:
Olivier Dondjio, Toni Karvonen
Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful and general framework for sample-efficient global optimization. Most BO methods rely on stationary Gaussian processes, implicitly assuming that an objective black-box function exhibits homogeneous smoothness across the input space. item.description:
Tuulia Tokola, Mohamed Fkirine, Lassi Paunonen
Motivated by the study of excitable control of infinite-dimensional linear systems, we investigate the global stability properties of a closed-loop system consisting of a stable linear infinite-dimensional plant and a non-monotone controller. item.description:

We consider the problem of learning microscopic traffic dynamics and reconstructing vehicle trajectories from section entry/exit timestamps (EET) recorded by cameras and from the positions of a probe vehicle leading the platoon. item.description:
Ying Liu, Raimundo Saona
Scoring rules are used to elicit probabilistic beliefs through payments that depend on reports and realised outcomes. We ask how these rules should be designed to induce truthful reporting and incentivise costly information acquisition when the agent is risk averse. item.description:
Oliver Heinzel, Smajil Halilovic, Thomas Hamacher, Michael Ulbrich
Common analytical design tools for Borehole Heat Exchanger (BHE) fields size the total drilling length for a given layout but do not optimize the positions of the boreholes. We introduce a framework (OptiGeoS) for the simultaneous, gradient-based optimization of the borehole length and the continuous borehole positions under groundwater advection. item.description:
Johann Cl{é}ment-Cottuz, Gilles Gasso, Maxime Berar
Multimarginal Optimal Transport (MOT) suffers from exponential computational and memory costs in the number of marginals, as transport plans are represented by high-dimensional tensors. item.description:

Missed Thrust Events (MTEs) are a major roadblock towards widespread adoption of low-thrust propulsion for deep space missions. Unplanned thruster outages have previously been difficult to directly incorporate in the preliminary mission design process, and current approaches mostly introduce robustness by conservative heuristics such as mandatory coasting arcs, which do not possess any safety guarantees, and usually only consider one missed-thrust event. item.title: Support monotonicity for quadratically regularized optimal transport
item.description:
Johannes Wiesel, Xingyu Xu
We study the support of the optimizer $π_\varepsilon$ of the quadratically regularized optimal transport problem for quadratic cost and compactly supported marginals. As $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, this support converges to the support of the Monge coupling. We investigate whether the regularized supports are nested as $\varepsilon $ decreases. Under regularity assumptions on the marginal densities, their domains, and the Brenier map, we establish interior support inclusions in every dimension.

It partitions the index set of all constraints into subsets of indices, called strings, allowing the user to apply operators successively along each string separately, and thus in parallel. item.title: The response field approach to path integral control
item.description:

This paper investigates non-linear path integral control problems within the response field formalism of nonequilibrium field theory. The aim of this work is exploratory, based on the identification of correspondences between backward adjoint processes and the response field of non-equilibrium statistical physics, whose properties have not been set out in an optimal control setting. item.title: First-Order Information from Noisy Comparison Oracles
item.description:
Qipei Chen, Katya Scheinberg, Zikai Xiong
We study stochastic and deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization problems where neither the functions nor their derivatives can be computed or estimated and the only information about the objective is available via pairwise comparisons. item.title: The Optimal D.C. Bound Is Dominated by the Reciprocal of the Lovász Theta Number
item.description:
Yuqin Ao, Yong Xia
We resolve a question left open by Anstreicher and Burer (J. Global Optim. 33, 299--312, 2005). For the standard quadratic formulation of the stability number, we prove that the optimal difference-of-convex (D.C.) bound is at most the reciprocal of the Lovász theta number. The dominance is strict whenever the Lovász theta number is not exact.

item.description:

item.title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
item.description:
Mohammed Baharoon, Sung Eun Kim, Mahmoud Hussain Alabbad, Lucas Bijnens, Ali Piracha et al.
Radiology reports describe findings in text only, without visually marking them on the scan, so readers cannot directly see which abnormality each reported finding refers to. We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted 3D segmentation model that segments findings described in a chest CT report. item.description:
